page.layout: Running head centred at top, page number top right. Two medallion portraits side by side at the top (left: Selimus; right: Amurath). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs. No notes in the margins, no footnotes.

main_text.l: SELIMVS huius nominis secundus, Turcarum Im-
perator, post mortem Solimani patris sui, aliquamdiu occul-
tatam in Hungaria, capta Zighet, imperio successit Mehe-
meti Bassæ industria, antequam patris mors patefacta esset.
Hic Aimanum qui in Arabia rebellauerat, armis compressit,
bellum Venetis intulit, rupto cum his fœdere{¹}, & multis locis
in Albania expugnatis, Insulam Cypriam occupauit anno sa-
lutis 1571. Tandem commissa pugna adversus confœdera-
tos, ingētem cladem accepit, classe à Christianis victa, sed pau-
lò post, eam restituit, fœdere rursus inito, cum republica Vene-
torum: & recuperatis in Africa, Aphrodisio & Guletta à Rege
Hispaniæ antea occupatis, mortuus est, anno salutis 1574. Porrò
hæc omnia quæ recensui, gesta sunt, dum lascivus Imperator
genio indulgeret, mulieribus & gulæ omnino deditus.
AMVRATH, huius nominis tertius, Selimi filius, crea-
tus est Turcarum Imperator, Imperióque potitus, post patrem
mortuum diebus octo, anno salutis humanæ 1574. Immani
& barbarogetis Turcicæ more, qui jamdiu invaluit, quinque fra-
tres eius (proh Deum atque hominum fidem) interfici iussit, ut
solus sine ullo metu & suspicione quæ reges plerumque comi-
tari solet, imperaret: & vitam ageret pacificam, & omnibus im-
pedimentis, quæ frequenter intellexerat posse intervenire inter
plures consortes & in eadem prope fortuna constitutos, immu-
nem. Imperium cœpit gubernare juvenis, annos natus viginti
octo: religionis Mahumetanæ imprimis studiosus, eíque vehe-
menter addictus, quem constat justitiæ mirum inmodum ob-
servantissimum, Solimani eius avi imitatorem esse.

page.notes: Medallion legends (part of the engravings, not running text): left portrait "SELIMVS" with "II" and "IMP. TVRC."; right portrait "AMVRATH" with "III. IMP. TVRC.". "fœdere{¹}": a small reference mark follows "fœdere" in the text, but no matching note is printed on this page. "ingētem": the macron over the e is faint; read as printed. "justitiæ": the word shows a small gap in the print; reading "iustitiæ" as printed, normalised to "justitiæ" under the i/j rule. Spelling kept as printed except u/v and i/j normalisation (e.g. "lascivus", "invaluit", "intervenire", "avi", "observantissimum").
